## Percentage change and multipliers {#ss8-percentages .growth-lesson .growth-percentages}

::: {.split .growth-percentage-layout}
::: {.column-block}
<h3>6% increase</h3>

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}

$$100\%+6\%=106\%$$

$$\text{Multiply by }\textcolor{#3b66a8}{1.06}$$

:::
:::
::: {.column-block}
<h3>12% decrease</h3>

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}

$$100\%-12\%=88\%$$

$$\text{Multiply by }\textcolor{#b55224}{0.88}$$

:::
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}

The same percentage change each period means multiplying the **current amount** by the same factor each time.

:::

::: notes

Ask students for both multipliers before the first click. Click 1 reveals 106% and 88%, with multipliers 1.06 and 0.88. Click 2 links repeated percentage change to a geometric model. A 6% increase adds 6% of the current amount each time, not a fixed dollar amount. Keep this to one or two minutes. The general rule is multiplier 1+p/100 for a p% increase and 1−p/100 for a p% decrease.

:::
